data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise Present Simple and Past Simple passive forms when the action or result is more important than the doer.
data.learningTitle: Using Present and Past Passive Forms
learningPoints: Form the Present Simple passive with am/is/are + past participle.
Form the Past Simple passive with was/were + past participle.
Use the passive when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
Use 'by' when the doer needs to be mentioned.
Keep tense information in the form of 'be'.
Distinguish active and passive sentence structure.

sections.explain: Use IS/ARE + past participle for Present Simple passive forms.

words.word: English is spoken in many countries.
English speaks in many countries.
English is speak in many countries.

sections.explain: Use WAS/WERE + past participle for Past Simple passive forms.

words.word: The bridge was built in 1998.
The bridge built in 1998.
The bridge was build in 1998.

sections.summary: Using a plural Present Simple passive.
sections.explain: Use ARE + past participle with a plural subject.

words.word: These cars are made in Japan.
These cars is made in Japan.
These cars are make in Japan.

sections.summary: Using a plural Past Simple passive.
sections.explain: Use WERE + past participle with a plural subject in the past.

words.word: The windows were cleaned yesterday.
The windows was cleaned yesterday.
The windows were clean yesterday by someone.

sections.explain: Use BY when it is useful to say who performed the action.

words.word: The novel was written by George Orwell.
The novel wrote by George Orwell.
The novel was wrote from George Orwell.

sections.summary: Using the passive when the doer is unimportant.
sections.explain: The passive focuses on the process or result rather than the person doing it.

words.word: The rubbish is collected every Tuesday.
They collect every Tuesday the rubbish is.
The rubbish collects every Tuesday.

sections.explain: TAKE has the past participle TAKEN in passive structures.

words.word: The photo was taken last summer.
The photo was took last summer.
The photo took last summer.

sections.explain: Put IS/ARE before the subject in a passive question.

words.word: Is this room used every day?
Does this room used every day?
Is this room use every day?

sections.explain: Put WAS/WERE before the subject in a Past Simple passive question.

words.word: Were the tickets sold online?
Did the tickets sold online?
Were the tickets sell online?

sections.explain: Use the passive when the receiver of the action is the topic.

words.word: The new hospital was opened last year.
The new hospital opened someone last year.
The new hospital was open by last year.
